clue.text: Turn red, black and green

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
lush vegetation is green and thriving

explanation.surface: A list of colours, or something changing from red through black to green.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read three colours in a row, but 'Turn red' is the definition and 'black and green' builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Going pink in the face from embarrassment is exactly what it means to colour up, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Disreputable singer overheard

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by the ear, so we want a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice, pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: A singer of poor reputation whose conversation someone happened to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The low-voiced singer is spelt BASS but said exactly like the adjective meaning low or morally unworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Base describes conduct that is morally low, contemptible and without honour, a close synonym.

clue.text: Squad uniform on dummy

parts.note: Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for U
a nit is a fool or dummy

explanation.surface: A team's kit being tried on a tailor's dummy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one piece placed 'on' another sits above it. 'Uniform' looks like clothing but is the radio-alphabet code word for one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a small organized group of soldiers or police working together, the same as a squad.

clue.text: Two-facedness of rich spy you almost corrupted

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped
corrupted means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A wealthy secret agent turned double agent, accused of duplicity.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed second-person pronoun joins two other words, and the nine letters are then shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being two-faced means professing one thing while doing another, which is the essence of hypocrisy.

clue.text: Mistake flower for flour product

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a blunder or embarrassing error
second meaning: a large crusty British loaf with diagonal slashes on top

explanation.surface: Someone confuses a garden flower with bread flour, a classic homophone mix-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface mistake is itself a bloomer; a plant that flowers is also a bloomer, a third meaning playing in the background. A bloomer is a type of British white loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a silly blunder in informal British English and a particular baked loaf of bread.

clue.text: British liner refurbished in European city

indicators.note: refurbishing a ship rebuilds and rearranges its fittings, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British ocean liner being refitted in a dockyard in some continental port.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is inland, so the shipyard picture is pure decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital of Germany, an example of a major city in Europe.

clue.text: Raised for the attention of clumsy fool

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the letters means reading them from the bottom up

parts.note: FAO is the abbreviation used on letters and memos for 'for the attention of'

explanation.surface: Something brought up for the notice of a bumbling idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: FAO is a common British office abbreviation written at the top of a letter to name its intended reader.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a big, awkward, stupid person, the very picture of a clumsy fool.

clue.text: Max's counterpart starts to support The Red Elvises' lead singer

parts.note: the opposite of max (maximum) is min (minimum)

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A musician named Max's opposite number opens for the frontman of the band The Red Elvises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead singer' looks like one phrase, but 'lead' is the last word whose first letter is taken, leaving just 'singer' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a medieval entertainer who sang or recited poetry, so a kind of singer.

clue.text: Supporter of sovereign, even if right became left

parts.note: surface reading: someone who backs the monarchy
setter's reading: swap the letter R for L and you get another word for a crown supporter, so the meaning survives the change

explanation.surface: A monarchist stays loyal to the crown even if their politics swung from right to left.
explanation.walkthrough: Right and left look political, but they stand for the letters R and L: change the first letter and LOYALIST still supports the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist is someone who backs a king or queen and the institution of monarchy.

clue.text: Captain who jumps over rope

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the commander of a ship or team
second meaning: a person skipping with a rope

explanation.surface: A ship's captain leaping over a coil of rope on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The rope fits the nautical scene, but here it is a skipping rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipper is an informal term for a ship's master or team leader, and literally someone who skips.

clue.text: Like supporter, cry when heart gets ripped out

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, and ripping it out removes the middle letter

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a team or star
the word with its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: A fan weeps when their team's heart is torn out by defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' seems to compare, but it is a verb meaning to be attracted to.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy someone or something is to find it appealing, an informal synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Citadel can convert into flat, perhaps

indicators.note: converting a building changes its layout, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A developer turning an old fortress into an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like housing, but it is the musical symbol that lowers a note.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation a flat, sharp or natural sign not in the key signature is called an accidental.

clue.text: Remove badly created AI

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to delete a poorly built artificial intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly created' reads as one phrase about the software, but 'badly' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or get rid of completely, a stronger synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Approximate maturity needed for coarse material

parts.note: a rough figure is an approximate one
age is maturity, years of growing up

explanation.surface: A recipe or process that needs ripening to produce a coarse fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approximate' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning not exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is coarse, fibrous plant matter in food that aids digestion, i.e. dietary fibre.

clue.text: Oscar wearing leather shoe without front for special event

indicators.note: lacking its front means the first letter is dropped
whatever wears clothing is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a moccasin is a soft leather shoe, minus its first letter
Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: A film-award winner in leather shoes for a gala night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the Academy Award, but it is the radio code word for one letter. It slips in near the end of the trimmed shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular event or celebration, especially a notable one.

clue.text: Perennial fantasy villain laid low

parts.note: orcs are monstrous villains in Tolkien and other fantasy
to lie low is to hide, so laid low is hid

explanation.surface: A recurring villain in a fantasy saga is finally brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial' looks like an adjective describing the villain, but it is a noun for a plant that lives for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Many orchids are long-lived flowering plants returning year after year, so an example of a perennial.

clue.text: Embrace a boring salad ingredient

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: cress is a peppery leaf used in salads
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to hug a dull salad vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull' but means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke or hold someone tenderly, close in sense to an embrace.

clue.text: Inexperienced English novelist

parts.note: green means new and untried
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A young, untested English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English' looks like it describes the novelist, but it supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was a twentieth-century writer of books such as Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.

clue.text: Food offered in boat and coach? Nice work if you can get it

definitions.text: Nice work if you can get it

parts.note: gravy is served at table from a gravy boat
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Meals served on boats and buses, which sounds like a cushy job.
explanation.walkthrough: The boat is a gravy boat, a jug-shaped dish, and 'coach' is the verb, not a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy train is an easy job or scheme that pays well for little effort, an idiomatic description.

clue.text: Ejected for quarrel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: expelled from the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ejected for quarrel' sounds like someone thrown out for fighting; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of spit means forced out of the mouth, and a minor squabble is also called by this word.

clue.text: Foreign character actor's name coming ahead of Jones

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet

definitions.text: actor's name coming ahead of Jones
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the front half of the hyphenated surname of the Welsh actress Catherine, whose name ends in Jones

explanation.surface: An exotic film actor billed above someone called Jones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a role in a film, but it means a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeta is the sixth letter of the Greek alphabet and the first part of Catherine Zeta-Jones's double-barrelled surname.

clue.text: Am I ahead of the game, buddy?

parts.note: taken as written
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Someone asking a friend whether they are winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead of the game' is an idiom for being in front, but here it just places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, borrowed into English as an informal word for a pal.

clue.text: Globe kept by Gorbachev

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it, so the letters sit within a word

parts.note: letters two to four of the name

explanation.surface: A globe that the Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev kept on his desk.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous birthmark-and-world picture is decoy; the answer sits right inside the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere or ball, and the globe of the world is a spherical body.

clue.text: One previously dated liberal, for instance

definitions.note: the phrase is adverbial; the answer is the noun it introduces

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a liberal helping is an ample one

explanation.surface: A former partner who was a political Liberal, cited as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' looks political, but it means generous or plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'for instance' introduces a case or illustration, which is what an example is.

clue.text: Some given no blessing or honour

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part taken from the run of words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Some people receive neither a blessing nor an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The negative 'no' seems to deny the honour, yet it supplies two of the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility or dignify them, a way to honour a person.

clue.text: Eg wide part of film's background

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket a wide, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach
second meaning: a non-speaking actor in a crowd scene

explanation.surface: A wide shot forming part of the backdrop of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wide' looks like a camera term, but it is the cricket delivery; cricket is a bat-and-ball sport popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs not scored off the bat are extras in cricket, and background film performers are extras too.
